outcome: Fetal occiput posterior (OP) position at birth
Duration of active phase of labor
Duration of the third stage of labor
Rate of neonatal addition to neonatal intensive care unit
cohort: The study included 180 primigravida women in labor with a single fetus and an approved occiput posterior (OP) position.
finding: The semi-prone and knee-chest maternal positions significantly increased the spontaneous rotation of the occiput to the anterior position and vaginal delivery rates, while also reducing the duration of the active phase of labor and low back pain after delivery compared to the supine position.
mod_finding: The rate of natural delivery was significantly higher in the semi-prone and knee-chest maternal positions compared to the control (supine) group.
